description: Deterministic synthetic fixtures for the M2-03 timestamp/score regression suite (tests/test_matching_regression.py), exercising the existing M2-02 match_cue baseline (src/audio_cue_locator/infrastructure/acoustic_matching/baseline.py) against docs/matching-contract.md and docs/matching-baseline.md, which this manifest does not redefine. Every array is a plain list of finite floats; the consuming test converts each to a CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC-conformant (mono, float32) numpy array itself -- this manifest does not declare its own sample rate, since the canonical sample rate is owned by CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC and must not be duplicated here. Each case's expected outcome and evidentiary values are derived analytically from docs/matching-baseline.md's documented algorithm (normalized cross-correlation via numpy.correlate 'valid' mode, integer-lag best-candidate search, and the deterministic degenerate-input table in its section 5), not from executing the suite.

cases.description: Cue embedded verbatim at a known early sample offset inside an otherwise silent source. The window at cue_start_sample is identical to the cue, so normalized cross-correlation reaches its Cauchy-Schwarz equality bound (score exactly 1.0); every other window either has ~zero energy (untouched silence) or a strict partial overlap that cannot be a positive scalar multiple of the cue (the cue has no zero-valued sample), so the maximum is unique at cue_start_sample.

A second, distinct known offset and a longer, differently-shaped cue, embedded near the end of a longer silent source, covering a different lag magnitude than found_offset_near_start. Same Cauchy-Schwarz uniqueness argument applies: the cue has no zero-valued sample, so only the exact placement is proportional to the cue.

A zero-sum alternating cue against a flat, non-silent source. dot(window, cue) is exactly value*(1-1+1-1) = 0 for every window of a constant source, at every lag, regardless of the constant's magnitude; both window and cue have nonzero energy, so the score is a genuine, non-defaulted 0.0 at every lag (not the degenerate-energy fallback), correctly resolving to no_match with diagnostic evidence retained, not an error.

A zero-energy (silent) cue against a non-silent source: normalized correlation is mathematically undefined (0/0) at every lag, so baseline.py deterministically defines every score as 0.0 without computing the non-silent branch at all, resolving to no_match, never a crash or a fabricated found.

A non-silent cue against an entirely silent source: every window has ~zero energy, so every lag is excluded from the non-silent scoring branch and the score stays at its initialized 0.0 for all lags, resolving to no_match with the earliest lag (sample 0) reported as the tied diagnostic best candidate.

The source is shorter than the cue: docs/matching-contract.md section 1 explicitly allows this as a valid canonicalized input, so match_cue returns no_match via an explicit early branch before any candidate window is evaluated. No diagnostic candidate exists at all in this case (unlike the other no_match cases above), so timestamp, score and both diagnostic fields all stay unset (None); only a non-null reason distinguishes this branch.
